cases.note: The loop iterates the same thresholds (PB→KB) in the same descending order with the same 'B' fallback and identical guard conditions as the original if/else chain, so unit selection is unchanged for every finite input. This is an equivalent refactor with no observable behavioural difference.

The core-schema explicit !!int pattern was changed from [-+]?0b[0-1]+ to [^-+]?0b[0-1]+, so explicitly tagged signed binary integers like '!!int -0b1010' now throw 'cannot resolve' instead of returning -10, while malformed input like '!!int 10b1010' is now silently resolved as 10. Both differences are caller-observable in the default CORE_SCHEMA.

cases.note: The change only renames `value` to `digits` and hoists `digits.slice(2)` into `rest`. `rest` is consumed solely by the 0b/0o/0x branches, where it is byte-for-byte the value the original computed inline via `value.slice(2)`, and the decimal fallback still parses the full string, so behaviour is identical for all inputs.

The diff replaces the typeof check with `true`, so the parse branch runs for any value with length > 0. Consequently ms(null) and ms(undefined) now throw a TypeError from reading .length instead of the documented validation Error, ms(['2 days']) coerces the array and returns 172800000 instead of throwing, and ms({length: 2}) returns undefined instead of throwing.
